question: Which of the following parts of the Constitution of India has been referred to as the 'conscience of the Indian Constitution'?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Fundamental Rights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights** are referred to as the '**conscience of the Indian Constitution**' because they embody the core values of liberty, equality, and justice.
 
• These rights are enshrined in **Part III of the Indian Constitution** and are considered essential for the holistic development of every citizen.
 
• They are **justiciable**, meaning they are legally enforceable by the judiciary, and citizens can approach the courts if their rights are violated.
